subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: What default recovery policy should OpenClaw use when the active session transcript is too large to safely repair/open on gateway restart?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the durable fix changes user-visible recovery semantics: quarantine/skip, truncate/compact, or opt-in-only behavior each has data retention and upgrade tradeoffs.

options.title: Default quarantine and doctor recovery
options.body: Before whole-file repair/open, detect oversized active transcripts, mark the session degraded, skip the crash loop, and surface a doctor/fix path that preserves the original file for operator recovery.

options.title: Bootstrap circuit breaker only
options.body: Land only the open bootstrap-marker cap and accept that oversized transcripts can still OOM until a later recovery design lands.

options.title: Opt-in compaction guard only
options.body: Rely on `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` and transcript rotation configuration, which avoids a default data-policy change but leaves existing default installs exposed.

recommendation.title: Default quarantine and doctor recovery
recommendation.body: Before whole-file repair/open, detect oversized active transcripts, mark the session degraded, skip the crash loop, and surface a doctor/fix path that preserves the original file for operator recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session/transcript merge history makes this the best available routing owner for the recovery-policy decision.
